name: Z/W Hopf rule
summary: A Z-spider and a W-spider connected by two wires disconnect.
description:
The W-spider (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg. A W-spider with no outputs is the state $|0\rangle$ (read as an effect, it is $\langle 0|$), which is the unit of the W-spider read as a 'merge'.

Copying a basis state with a Z-spider and merging the two copies with a W-spider kills $|1\rangle$ (two excitations cannot be merged) and keeps $|0\rangle$, so the composite is $|0\rangle\langle0|$. This is axiom 6c of Hadzihasanovic's ZW-calculus. More generally, any number $n \geq 2$ of parallel wires between a W-spider and a Z-spider can be cut ($\mathrm{lp}^n$), and in the thesis the Z-spider may carry any label $r$ (rule $loop$).
parameter_notes: Shown with two parallel wires; holds for any number $n \geq 2$ of wires.
